title: Strawberry Lemonade Cookies for Black History Month
h1: Black History Month: Infused Strawberry Lemonade Cookies
metaDescription: Easy two-tone strawberry lemonade cookies made from cake mix and cannabutter, plus a short, factual look at Black history in cannabis and ways to take part.
excerpt: A two-tone cake-mix cookie made with cannabutter, paired with a short look at how cannabis enforcement fell on Black communities and how you can support Black-owned businesses.

body:
Black History Month is a good time for the cannabis world to look at who paid the price for prohibition. These two-tone strawberry lemonade cookies, made from cake mix and cannabutter, give adults 21 and older a bright, easy bake to share while you talk about it.

## Why Black History Month matters in cannabis

Federal prohibition traces back to the 1937 Marihuana Tax Act. Its chief promoter, Federal Bureau of Narcotics head Harry Anslinger, spread racist and false claims about the drug, though historians still debate how much race drove the law itself. In 1970, the Controlled Substances Act grouped marijuana with heroin and LSD in Schedule I.

The enforcement record is clearer. When the ACLU studied FBI arrest data from 2010 to 2018, it found that in 2018, Black Americans were arrested for marijuana possession at 3.64 times the rate of white Americans. Yet the two groups use marijuana about equally. Nationwide, 2018 alone brought almost 700,000 marijuana arrests. Our feature on [Black History Month and cannabis](/blog/celebrating-black-history-month/) goes deeper.

## Michigan today: equity and old records

Michigan's adult-use law came by ballot in 2018 and has applied since December 6 of that year. Legal sales raised two equity questions: who gets to own and work in the industry, and what happens to people with old marijuana records. Our guides to [cannabis social equity](/blog/cannabis-social-equity/) and [clearing an old marijuana record in Michigan](/blog/michigan-marijuana-expungement/) explain where each stands as of October 2026.

## How you can take part

- **Learn the history.** Read beyond February, starting with the people who were arrested and the people who pushed for change.
- **Shop Black-owned businesses.** Look for Black-owned bakeries, restaurants and shops in your community, all year.
- **Support local organizations.** Find groups working on record clearing, reentry and reform, and ask how you can help; our roundup of [advocacy organizations](/blog/cannabis-advocacy-organizations/) is a place to start.

## Dosing: work out mg per cookie first

Divide the THC in the cannabutter you'll use by the number of cookies. This recipe makes about 32 cookies with 2/3 cup of butter in total. Say your cannabutter works out to 39 to 45 mg per tablespoon at most, as in the worked example from our [cannabutter recipe](/blog/canna-butter-recipe/). One tablespoon in each dough then adds 78 to 90 mg, or roughly 2.4 to 2.8 mg per cookie; use plain butter for the rest. Count the cookies you actually bake and redo the math, since fewer cookies means more THC in each. An edible may not show its effects for 2 hours, and they can run 4 to 12 hours, so have one cookie and be patient. Our [THC dosage guide](/blog/thc-dosage-guide/) explains starting amounts.

## What you need for strawberry lemonade cookies

- 1 box (13 to 15 ounces) each of strawberry and lemon cake mix
- 4 large eggs, 2 per dough
- 2/3 cup melted butter in total, part cannabutter and the rest plain
- 2 tablespoons flour, 1 per dough, to help the soft dough hold its shape
- Optional glaze: 1 cup powdered sugar whisked with 1 1/2 to 2 tablespoons lemon juice

## How to bake two-tone cookies

Mix each dough in its own bowl, with half the cannabutter in each, until no streaks remain. Chill the doughs for 15 minutes if they're sticky. Press a tablespoon of each together into one ball and bake 2 inches apart at 350°F for 8 to 10 minutes. Pull them while the centers still look soft; they firm up as they cool. Drizzle on the glaze once they're completely cool.

## Storage and labeling

Kept in an airtight tin at room temperature, the cookies last up to about a week. Write "contains THC," the mg per cookie and the bake date on the tin, and store it high up, apart from everyday snacks and away from kids and pets. Michigan lets adults 21 and older give up to 2.5 ounces of cannabis to other adults 21 and older, as long as nothing is received in return and the gift isn't advertised. So these cookies are for sharing, not selling. If a child eats one, call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222, or 911 in an emergency; if a pet does, call your veterinarian or an animal poison control center.

faq.q: Why is Black History Month connected to cannabis reform?
faq.a: Because the costs of prohibition fell unevenly. ACLU research covering 2010 to 2018 found that in 2018, Black Americans were arrested for marijuana possession at 3.64 times the rate of white Americans, even though use rates were similar. Equity licensing and record-clearing efforts grew out of that history, which makes February a natural time to learn about it.

faq.q: What dose of THC does each cookie carry?
faq.a: That comes from your own cannabutter. Multiply the tablespoons you use by your butter's mg per tablespoon, then divide by the number of cookies. With butter at 39 to 45 mg a tablespoon at most, 2 tablespoons spread over 32 cookies come to roughly 2.4 to 2.8 mg each. Real batches usually come in lower, but plan servings from the higher figure.

faq.q: Can I use canna-oil instead of cannabutter?
faq.a: Yes. Cake-mix cookies often call for oil, so canna-oil swaps in easily: use 1/3 cup of fat per box, part infused and the rest plain. A neutral oil or coconut oil keeps the fruit flavors bright, while a strong olive oil can clash. The dosing math is the same, using your oil's mg per tablespoon.

sources.label: ACLU: A Tale of Two Countries: Racially Targeted Arrests in the Era of Marijuana Reform (April 2020)
Fisher G., Racial Myths of the Cannabis War, Boston University Law Review 101:933 (2021)
University of Chicago Law Review Online: The Unconstitutional Racial Animus Behind Federal Marijuana Criminalization (2022)
Michigan Judicial Institute, Controlled Substances Benchbook, sec. 8.14: Scope of the MRTMA
Public Health Agency of Canada: Council of Chief Medical Officers of Health statement on cannabis extracts, edibles and topicals (2020)
America's Poison Centers: Frequently asked questions (pet poisonings)

ingredients: 1 box (13 to 15 ounces) strawberry cake mix
1 box (13 to 15 ounces) lemon cake mix
2/3 cup melted butter in total: cannabutter plus plain butter (see the note)
Optional glaze: 1 cup powdered sugar and 1 1/2 to 2 tablespoons lemon juice
steps: Get the oven to 350°F and cover two baking sheets with parchment.
In one bowl, mix the strawberry cake mix, 2 eggs, 1/3 cup of the melted butter blend (with half the cannabutter) and 1 tablespoon flour until smooth.
In a second bowl, do the same with the lemon cake mix and the rest of the eggs, butter blend and flour.
Chill both doughs for 15 minutes if they feel sticky.
Scoop 1 tablespoon of each dough, press them together into one ball and set the balls 2 inches apart.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes, until the edges are set and the centers still look soft. Cool for 5 minutes on the sheet, then on a rack.
Whisk the glaze, drizzle it over the cooled cookies and let it set. Store airtight with a label.
recipe.dosingNote: An estimate: assuming cannabutter at 39 to 45 mg per tablespoon at most, 1 tablespoon in each dough (2 in all) adds 78 to 90 mg, spread over 32 cookies at roughly 2.4 to 2.8 mg apiece. Real batches usually come in lower, because the flower's true strength and the losses in decarbing and infusing set the real figure, and fewer cookies means more THC in each. Start with a single cookie and wait at least 2 hours before another. Label the tin and keep it where little hands and pets can't reach.

claims.claim: Federal prohibition traces back to the 1937 Marihuana Tax Act
claims.source: UChicago Law Review Online (Clark-Ansani, July 29, 2022): the Act's penalties 'effectively made it illegal'; Fisher, 101 B.U. L. Rev. 933 (2021): 'the first federal assault on marijuana'. Both opened 2026-10-24.

claims.claim: Harry Anslinger, head of the Federal Bureau of Narcotics, was the Act's chief promoter
claims.source: UChicago Law Review Online: 'the pioneer of the act', 'the head of the Federal Bureau of Narcotics'; Fisher p. 935: 'an architect and vocal promoter of the Marihuana Tax Act of 1937' (PDF text extracted 2026-10-24).

claims.claim: Anslinger spread racist and false claims about the drug
claims.source: UChicago Law Review Online: he 'propagated racist and false statements about marijuana'.

claims.claim: Historians still debate how much race drove the 1937 law itself
claims.source: Fisher 2021 abstract: modern histories that draw from Anslinger's personal racism the conclusion that he deployed race 'often go astray'; the race-animus premise is 'misguided'.

claims.claim: In 1970 the Controlled Substances Act put marijuana in Schedule I with heroin and LSD
claims.source: UChicago Law Review Online: the CSA 'made it a Schedule I drug along with other drugs such as heroin and LSD'.

claims.claim: ACLU, FBI data 2010-2018: Black Americans arrested for marijuana possession at 3.64 times the rate of white Americans
claims.source: ACLU, A Tale of Two Countries (Apr. 16, 2020): 'On average, a Black person is 3.64 times more likely to be arrested for marijuana possession than a white person'; data 2010-2018. Opened 2026-10-24.

claims.claim: Black and white Americans use marijuana at about equal rates
claims.source: ACLU 2020: 'even though Black and white people use marijuana at similar rates'.

claims.claim: Almost 700,000 marijuana arrests nationwide in 2018
claims.source: ACLU 2020: 'almost 700,000'.

claims.claim: Equity licensing and record-clearing efforts grew out of the enforcement history (FAQ)
claims.source: ACLU 2020 ties its call for reassessing marijuana convictions and legalization 'with racial equity at the foundation' to the arrest disparities. No Michigan program detail is stated (not in law-facts); the article links the planned equity and expungement guides instead.

claims.claim: Michigan's adult-use law passed by ballot in 2018 and took effect December 6, 2018
claims.source: facts/law-facts.json mi-au-age (MJI Controlled Substances Benchbook 8.14).

claims.claim: Cannabutter at 'up to 39 mg per tablespoon, as in the worked example from our cannabutter recipe'; 2 tbsp = 78 mg = about 2.4 mg per cookie (body, FAQ, dosing note)
claims.fix: The cannabutter example's ceiling is 13 to 15 mg per teaspoon (630 mg over 48 or 42 tsp), which is 39 to 45 mg per tablespoon, so 39 was the low end of the ceiling. Now 39 to 45 mg/tbsp at most, 78 to 90 mg per batch, about 2.4 to 2.8 mg per cookie (78/32 = 2.44, 90/32 = 2.81), and readers are told to count the cookies they actually bake.
claims.source: site/src/content/blog/canna-butter-recipe.json potency worksheet; arithmetic.

claims.claim: Dosing note: 'Expect a little less in practice'
claims.fix: No source sizes the loss; reworded to 'Real batches usually come in lower', naming potency, decarb and infusion losses and batch size.
claims.source: Task dosing-note rule; canna-butter-recipe worksheet (ceiling assumes full transfer).

claims.claim: Edibles can take up to 2 hours to show effects, which can last 4 to 12 hours
claims.source: CCMOH statement, Public Health Agency of Canada (Jan. 6, 2020): 'It may take up to 2 hours to feel the effects ... The effects from edible cannabis last 4 to 12 hours'. Opened 2026-10-24.

claims.claim: Dosing note: 'allow 2 hours before another' cookie
claims.fix: Changed to 'wait at least 2 hours': the same statement says full effects can take up to 4 hours.
claims.source: CCMOH 2020: 'up to 4 hours to feel the full effects'.

claims.claim: Cake mix comes in boxes of about 15 ounces (body and recipe card)
claims.fix: Changed to '13 to 15 ounces' in all three places: Betty Crocker boxes shrank from 15.25 to 13.25 oz.
claims.source: Mouse Print, 'Here We Shrink Again - Early Fall 2023' (Sept. 18, 2023), https://www.mouseprint.org/?p=20410, opened 2026-10-24.

claims.claim: Recipe yields about 32 two-tone cookies (1 tbsp of each dough per cookie) with 2/3 cup butter in total
claims.fix: Kept as an estimate; the body now tells readers to count their own batch before working out the dose.
claims.source: Arithmetic: a 13.25-15.25 oz mix plus 2 eggs, 1/3 cup butter and 1 tbsp flour is roughly 560-615 g of dough, about 33-36 level tablespoons per dough.

claims.claim: Bake 2 inches apart at 350 F for 8 to 10 minutes; cookies keep about a week airtight at room temperature; 1/3 cup fat per box when swapping in canna-oil
claims.source: Standard cake-mix cookie method (1 box, 2 eggs, 1/3 cup fat); culinary guidance, not a regulated claim.

claims.claim: Michigan lets adults 21+ gift cannabis to other adults 21+ 'provided they get nothing back'
claims.fix: Added the conditions law-facts states: up to 2.5 ounces, nothing received in return, and the gift is not advertised.
claims.source: facts/law-facts.json mi-au-gifting (MCL 333.27955(1)(d), via MJI benchbook 8.14).

claims.claim: If a child or pet eats a cookie, call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222
claims.fix: The number is right for people; for pets, America's Poison Centers says member centers need not take pet calls and points to a veterinarian or animal poison center. Now: child, call 1-800-222-1222 or 911 in an emergency; pet, call a veterinarian or an animal poison control center. Source added.
claims.source: CDC Cannabis FAQ (Jan. 31, 2025): 'call a poison control center at ... 1-800-222-1222', 'In case of emergency, call 9-1-1'; America's Poison Centers FAQ, https://www.poisonhelp.org/faq, both opened 2026-10-24.

claims.claim: High Society facts
claims.source: None stated: no stores, staff, events, donations, discounts, equity status, products or shop links.

review.factCheckNotes: Fact-check 2026-10-24: 20 claims checked, 6 fixed (box size, cannabutter ceiling and per-cookie math, 'a little less', wait time, gifting conditions, pet poisoning). All cited URLs opened except the MJI benchbook, which law-facts lists as verified. Added the America's Poison Centers FAQ as a source. Cross-batch sweep 2026-10-24 (orchestrator, after the fact-check workflow): The ACLU's 2020 report (A Tale of Two Countries, PDF Table 6, read 2026-10-24) gives 3.31 for 2010 and 3.64 for 2018: 3.64 is the 2018 ratio, not a 2010-2018 average, so the year is now stated.
review.writerNotes: Michigan social equity licensing and expungement are not in facts/law-facts.json, so the article states no law on either and links the planned guides /blog/cannabis-social-equity/ and /blog/michigan-marijuana-expungement/ (both carry their own sources). The FAQ idea about clearing convictions was left out for the same reason. No High Society staff, events, donations, discounts or equity status are claimed. ACLU figure reworded so it does not repeat the phrasing used in /blog/cannabis-social-equity/ and /blog/celebrating-black-history-month/.
